revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown was mislabelled: a light check surfaced the official DGI e-SISIC portal. Fetched and confirmed via the Ministère des Finances du Niger and DGI Niger websites. The portal has been operational since 13 September 2019, enabling online tax declaration and e-payment, and was formally launched by the Minister of Finance in 2021. Score raised from 0 to 4 (Yes).
revised_comments: Niger's Direction Générale des Impôts (DGI) operates the e-SISIC portal (Système Informatisé de Suivi des Impôts et des Contribuables), an official government platform enabling taxpayers to file tax returns and pay taxes electronically. Operational since 13 September 2019 and accessible via impots.gouv.ne, the service covers declaration and payment for large enterprises and other taxpayer categories, with accounts activated using a taxpayer identification number issued by the DGI.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: [Adjusted from 1 to 0: no source URL available] Value=1 (no evidence): Looked for Niger government programs paying salaries/social transfers via mobile money/bank digital channels; no credible Niger-specific evidence found in accessible sources. (Note: regional STAR-UEMOA supports treasuries but does not itself evidence active G2P use in Niger.)
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown was mislabelled: a light check surfaced authoritative World Bank and IMF evidence of active G2P digitisation activity in Niger. The World Bank's Sahel Adaptive Social Protection Program has supported a pilot digital-payments programme (with CGAP) and modernisation of the payment system for the Registre Social Unifié; the IMF (2023) notes a government roadmap adopted in 2020 for complete digitalisation of government payments, not yet fully implemented; WFP/UNCDF piloted digitisation of social transfers in the Maradi and Zinder regions. This is limited/pilot use rather than active nationwide use, so score raised from 0 to 2 (Limited Use).
revised_comments: Niger has a government roadmap, adopted in 2020, for the complete digitalisation of government payments, but implementation remains partial. Digital government-to-person disbursement is at the pilot stage: the World Bank-financed Sahel Adaptive Social Protection Program has supported preparation of a digital-payments pilot for social transfers (with CGAP) and modernisation of the treasury payment system linked to the Registre Social Unifié, while WFP and UNCDF have piloted digitisation of monetary social transfers in the Maradi and Zinder regions. Nationwide, active use of digital channels for G2P disbursement remains limited rather than the norm.

Definition: Whether consumer protection legislation or regulations specifically address digital payment services, covering disclosure requirements, liability allocation for unauthorized transactions, error resolution procedures, and user rights.
Comments: Value=0 (unknown): Searched for Niger-specific payment consumer protection rules (dispute resolution, error resolution timelines, e-money customer funds safeguarding disclosures) in primary sources; did not find a clear payments-focused consumer protection framework for Niger/UEMOA suitable to score confidently.
redteam_note: Scored 0/Unknown with no source — confirm it is truly unknown, not just unresearched. No data year recorded — provenance/recency unknown.
revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown was mislabelled: a light check surfaced BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 (effective 23 January 2024), the regional regulation governing payment services across the UMOA/WAEMU zone including Niger, applicable to banks, payment institutions, e-money institutions and microfinance institutions. It includes provisions on client-fund segregation ('cantonnement') and strong customer authentication, which are consumer-protection-relevant, though the fetched text does not confirm dedicated dispute-resolution/liability-allocation clauses, and coverage is regional rather than Niger-specific. Score raised from 0 to 2 (Partial) with medium confidence; flagged for human review to confirm the extent of dispute-resolution and liability provisions in the full Instruction text.
revised_comments: Digital payment services in Niger are regulated regionally under BCEAO Instruction No. 001-01-2024 (effective 23 January 2024), which applies to banks, payment institutions, electronic money institutions and microfinance institutions across the West African Monetary Union. The Instruction requires segregation of client funds from institutional funds and mandates strong customer authentication for payment transactions, providing a degree of consumer protection. There is no Niger-specific consumer protection law dedicated to digital payments, and the full extent of provisions on dispute resolution, error correction and liability allocation for unauthorised transactions has not been independently confirmed.

revised_comments: BCEAO, the regional central bank and payment systems regulator for Niger and the other UEMOA member states, publishes an annual report on financial market infrastructures and payment instruments and services, most recently covering 2022-2023. This report discloses participant numbers and transaction volumes and values for the SICA-UEMOA clearing system and STAR-UEMOA settlement system, in which Niger's public treasury and banks participate, alongside BCEAO's own annual report. Reporting is conducted at the regional rather than Niger-specific level.

revision_notes: Original score of 0/Unknown was mislabelled: a light check surfaced Niger's Cadre National de Concertation sur l'Inclusion Financière (CNCFI), established under the 2019-2023 National Financial Inclusion Strategy and officially launched in September 2021, with UNCDF as secretariat. It comprises four working groups covering donor coordination, regulation (led by BCEAO, addressing consumer protection and interoperability), digital finance and innovation (led by ANSI, targeting women, youth and MSMEs, and digital G2P/NG2P payments), and market monitoring. This is a genuine multi-stakeholder inclusion-oriented coordination body touching payment-system regulation and inclusion, but it is a national policy coordination framework rather than the formal governance structure of a specific payment scheme/operator, so evidence supports 'Partial' rather than 'Yes'. Score raised from 0 to 2.
revised_comments: Niger's Cadre National de Concertation sur l'Inclusion Financière (CNCFI), created under the National Financial Inclusion Strategy (2019-2023) and launched in September 2021, brings together government, private-sector and development-partner stakeholders, with UNCDF acting as secretariat. Its four working groups address donor coordination, financial-sector regulation (led by BCEAO, including consumer protection and interoperability issues), digital finance and innovation (led by the Agence Nationale pour la Société de l'Information, targeting women, youth and micro and small enterprises, and covering digitisation of G2P and non-government-to-person payments), and market monitoring. This provides a degree of inclusive, multi-stakeholder input into payment and financial-inclusion policy, though it functions as a national coordination platform rather than formal governance of an individual payment scheme.
